children: has reached agreement with Trinidad and Tobago's National Gas Company on terms for natural gas supplies from the offshore Aphrodite field, ending a dispute over the price of gas from the development that had delayed the ​project, NGC's chairman told Reuters on Wednesday.

The agreement clears the way for development ‌of the field, with first production expected in Q2 2027, Gerald Ramdeen said, adding that the revised deal significantly improved the economics for ​NGC compared with terms that had been under discussion before Shell

The Aphrodite deal is expected to provide a modest boost to Trinidad's gas supply, as the country's energy ‌sector struggles ⁠with years of declining production that have reduced liquefied natural gas exports and forced the closure of several petrochemical plants.
Separately, Ramdeen said NGC has signed an agreement with EOG Resources
to purchase the company's share of gas from the Coconut project offshore Trinidad.

title: Shell and Trinidad agree on Aphrodite gas supply terms, clearing way for project
